review.purpose: Keep candidate, clean, allowlisted, empty and missing source populations distinct before prioritizing findings.
review.finding: Five source inputs remain in the audit. The synthetic candidate file returns TRUE; ordinary text, the allowlisted documentation placeholder and empty text return FALSE; SQL NULL remains unknown. The experiment preserves this audit exactly. No-match is explicitly not proof of safety, and no credential validity is tested.

review.purpose: Retain redacted evidence while changing only the review threshold, and test offset limitations separately.
review.finding: Four materialized findings contain no complete synthetic value. Raising confidence from 0.70 to 0.90 selects AWS and Slack while retaining npm and generic findings below threshold; scores are heuristics rather than probabilities. The separate repeated-match probe returns two rows at the same byte offset 7, so offsets cannot deduplicate occurrences. UTF-8 offsets and exact scalar/table input agreement are checked.

review.purpose: Use the curated registry to annotate findings without dropping unknown providers or treating representative confidence as an observed score.
review.finding: The eleven-rule registry is smaller than the embedded engine. A left join preserves the npm finding with NULL metadata and labels its reporting group explicitly. Actual generic confidence differs from the registry representative value. Both selected and below-threshold populations sum to all four findings, even when selected counts for Generic and the unregistered group fall to zero.
